scope: Standing exterior at Tytuvėnai. The monastery house consists of three two-storey brick wings of unequal mass, a rectangular cloister court and a low glazed link along the church. The brick wings have pitched clay-tile roofs.
geometryBasis: The mapped feature is localized in the geographic reference frame. The shared relation is split at the courtyard and church junctions using the heritage inventory.
sectionBasis: The monastery house consists of three two-storey brick wings of unequal mass, a rectangular cloister court and a low glazed link along the church. The brick wings have pitched clay-tile roofs.
limitations: The official register gives three attached two-storey wings and court dimensions near 16.5 m by 10.8 m. The mapped outline constrains the exterior and the wing roofs are fitted to its courtyard junctions.
The current mortar color, levels and exact fenestration are estimated. The west stepped gable follows the register description.

sources.use: Written heritage register inventory and section descriptions.
sources.controls: Three-aisled church with exposed brick and Gothic openings to the sides, a pale Baroque west facade and twin stepped towers, high main gable roof, lower lean-to aisles and a curved eastern end.

sources.use: The pilgrimage centre documents restoration of the church facades after the 2012 fire. The selected 2008 images guide historic form. Use published restoration facts for current scope and record any finish estimates.
The independently listed courtyard gallery is a current conservation project.
